abstract: TGF-{beta} signaling through SMAD transcription factors governs development and tissue homeostasis. Most disease-associated SMAD4 mutations cause loss of function, but five germline variants at only two positions in the MH2 domain, Arg496 and Ile500, instead cause Myhre syndrome, a rare condition inducing pathway dysregulation. We show that the two most common Myhre variants form more stable heterotrimers with SMAD3 than wild-type SMAD4, with affinities increasing two- to threefold and complex half-lives lengthening about fivefold. Cryo-EM reconstructions and twelve crystal structures show that a few interfacial hydrogen bonds shorten to 2.5 [A], reorganizing the binding interface. Our models also identified the SMAD4 C-terminus bound oriented resembling a phosphorylated R-SMAD tail, and two non-equivalent SMAD3 N-termini observed in the absence of cofactors. To the extent that these structural features reflect the cellular environment, they provide a mechanistic basis for the altered signaling dynamics observed in Myhre syndrome and outline concrete avenues for pharmacologically targeting these stabilized complexes.
